tasks.title: Tier-1 replay for K arms

report.outcome: Tier-1 replay over 6 sessions × 2 cuts ($0.42): A 96% retention at 88% sent, K 87% at 68%, K+/K+D 88% at 63%, versus C 70% at 53%. Losses: values in function bodies of skeletonized code reads, text in trimmed bash dumps and folded thinking.
decisions: K+D equals K+ in replay — birth skeletons only differ live, where results arrive fresh one by one
open: Probe set counts incidental text (rules quoted in a bash dump) as constraints — penalizes any trimming

tasks.title: Tier-2 live runs + analysis + verdict

blocks.detail: DeepSeek returns 402 Insufficient Balance; the user must top up the DeepSeek account (about $5 needed) before the remaining 45 tier-2 runs can execute

report.outcome: 50 live runs ($7.58): all arms 50/50 pass, 0 violations; K+/K+D/K+N cut peak context 89k → 45–53k but cost $0.156–0.174 vs $0.121, cache 96.4% → 90–93%, rereads 1.7 → 4–6; K alone ~no effect. Verdict written to the analysis README.
decisions: Keep A as default; thin:"open" only as an opt-in budget guard — halves peak context but costs 17–44% more via cache breaks and rereads
Drop thin:"orientation" and birthSkeleton — no live benefit
open: exp/orientation-modes not pushed
